R-ops-1 (The switch to Paylane has no way back) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-ops-2 (Nobody would see the settlement worker fail) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence:
The Stripe client is deleted and replaced by the Paylane client in the same
release. There is no switch between the two: keeping both would double the
code to maintain. The Stripe account is closed the day after the release.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: All traffic moves at deploy
findings.recommendation: Keep a way back until Paylane is proven in production: keep the Stripe client behind a configuration switch (or a percentage rollout) for at least one release cycle, and keep the Stripe account open until the switch has been off for that period and the first settlements have run cleanly. State in the design the rollback procedure (flip the switch, or redeploy the previous version while Stripe is still open) and the criterion for closing the Stripe account. Scenario that fails today: Paylane has an outage or the new client mis-captures payments on day two; deploys are weekly, the Stripe account is already closed, so redeploying the previous version cannot restore card payments and checkout stays down.
findings.title: The switch to Paylane has no way back

findings.evidence:
A new worker, `settlement-worker`, runs at 02:00, fetches the day's Paylane
payments and matches them to orders. It runs as a Kubernetes CronJob and
writes its result to the database.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: A worker settles payments nightly
findings.recommendation: Decide how an operator learns that the worker failed or did not run: alert on a failed or missed CronJob run (or a "last successful settlement" timestamp/metric checked against its schedule), log the start and the outcome of each run with counts (payments fetched, matched, unmatched), and state whether a failed run can be re-run safely for the same day. Scenario that fails today: the Paylane API is unreachable at 02:00 or the job crashes; nothing is written, no alert fires (the only alert in the spec is for an unmatched payment), and the day's payments stay unreconciled without anyone knowing.
findings.title: Nobody would see the settlement worker fail
